canonical_statement: The post hoc analysis evaluated whether baseline QoL-B-RSS symptom burden was associated with differential responses to florensocatib and inhaled tobramycin in adults with bronchiectasis.
The analysis used data from two multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials conducted in China: SAVE-BE and TORNASOL.

SAVE-BE included adult outpatients aged at least 18 years with HRCT-confirmed clinically significant bronchiectasis, at least 2 exacerbations in the prior 12 months, BMI at least 18 kg/m2, and daily spontaneous sputum production.
TORNASOL enrolled patients aged 18 to 75 years with symptomatic HRCT-confirmed bronchiectasis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation, and at least 1 exacerbation in the prior 2 years.
SAVE-BE randomized 224 patients; 107 (47.8%) had high symptom burden and 117 (52.2%) had low symptom burden using the study cutoff.
TORNASOL randomized 357 patients; 152 (42.6%) had high symptom burden and 205 (57.4%) had low symptom burden; outcome analyses followed the parent trial modified intention-to-treat population.

population.label: TORNASOL adults with bronchiectasis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection

canonical_statement: SAVE-BE randomized participants 1:1:1 to 20 mg florensocatib, 40 mg florensocatib, or placebo for 24 weeks; the two florensocatib doses were pooled for the post hoc analyses.
SAVE-BE used a placebo control with concealed allocation and participant/investigator blinding.
TORNASOL randomized participants 1:1 to nebulized tobramycin 300 mg twice daily in two 28-day on/off cycles totaling 16 weeks.
TORNASOL used 5 mL saline placebo twice daily on the same on/off schedule, with concealed allocation and participant/investigator blinding.
QoL-B-RSS was scored from 0 to 100 with lower scores indicating greater respiratory symptom severity; the MCID was 8 points.

outcome.definition: 0-100; lower scores indicate greater severity; MCID 8 points

canonical_statement: Patients were stratified as high symptom burden when baseline QoL-B-RSS was <60 and low symptom burden when it was >=60; the cutoff was based on trial medians rounded to 60 for clinical practicality.
Bronchiectasis exacerbations required at least 3 symptoms for longer than 48 hours requiring antibiotics; severe exacerbations required hospitalization.

outcome.definition: Exacerbation required at least 3 symptoms for >48 hours requiring antibiotics; severe exacerbations required hospitalization.

canonical_statement: SAVE-BE used negative-binomial generalized additive models for exacerbation frequency and Cox models for time to first exacerbation; ANCOVA evaluated changes in FEV1, sputum measures, and QoL-B-RSS.

TORNASOL used generalized additive modeling for the relationship between baseline QoL-B-RSS and treatment effect and mixed-effects models for QoL-B-RSS changes, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.
In SAVE-BE, pooled florensocatib reduced annualized exacerbation frequency versus placebo (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.33-0.67; p<0.0001).

In placebo arms, approximately 75% of patients with high baseline symptom burden remained high-burden throughout visits in both SAVE-BE and TORNASOL; low-burden classification remained in approximately 80% in SAVE-BE and >90% in TORNASOL.

The authors concluded that baseline symptom burden may identify differential responses to anti-inflammatory versus anti-infective therapies in bronchiectasis, but characterized the findings as hypothesis-generating and requiring prospective validation.

The authors proposed that lower-symptom patients may preferentially benefit from florensocatib for exacerbation prevention, whereas higher-symptom patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection may obtain greater symptomatic relief from inhaled tobramycin.

The post hoc analysis combined two randomized trials with different designs, populations, follow-up durations, and endpoint definitions, limiting direct cross-trial comparison and making the findings exploratory.
Dichotomizing baseline QoL-B-RSS at 60 may have lost information; continuous analyses were consistent with the main findings but showed no significant interactions.
In TORNASOL, baseline QoL-B-RSS was used both for stratification and as an endpoint, creating potential circularity for symptom-related outcomes despite baseline adjustment.

The SAVE-BE post hoc analysis pooled the 20 mg and 40 mg florensocatib doses because of limited sample size, potentially masking dose-specific effects and leaving lung-function and quality-of-life analyses underpowered.
SAVE-BE did not collect baseline BSI or bacterial colonization status, restricting interaction analyses.
The composite QoL-B-RSS may have limited sensitivity for subtle or domain-specific effects of anti-inflammatory therapy.
